name: IN-09
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about fifteen points Republican and the seat is held by a Republican incumbent
Erin Houchin has a massive financial edge: $2.2M raised and $929K on hand versus about $203K raised for Brad Meyer
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances at only about 3%
No public polls or expert ratings exist, so the race draws little outside attention or spending
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Republican lean, Houchin's roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and market pricing near three percent for Democrats all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and no polling or expert ratings suggest a competitive dynamic.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Houchin or a major campaign misstep could narrow the margin, though the structural lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 9th District, in the state's southern region, carries a strong Republican lean of roughly fifteen points on the partisan index. Republican incumbent Erin Houchin is seeking re-election and has built a dominant financial position, raising about $2.2 million with roughly $929,000 on hand. Democratic nominee Brad Meyer has raised about $203,000 with under $30,000 available, and Libertarian Tonya Hudson is on the ballot with negligible funding.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on the district's lean, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price Democratic chances at around three percent. With the incumbent well-funded in a favorable district and no evidence of a serious challenge emerging, this race rates as safe for Republicans, with the main question being the size of the winning margin rather than the winner.
